name: claudes
description: Keep several Claude Code accounts side by side and open a terminal on any of them with one click. Conversations, history and logins never cross between accounts; your settings, skills and MCP servers stay shared, and ClaudeS never writes to your Claude Code installation. Requires the Claude Code CLI (the `claude` command), installed separately: the Claude Code extension alone is not enough. Independent project, not affiliated with Anthropic.

claudes.profilesRoot.markdownDescription: Folder where new accounts are created. Leave empty to place them beside your Claude Code configuration, in a folder of ours: `~/.claudes` next to `~/.claude`. Never inside it, so uninstalling leaves nothing behind in another program's folder. Supports `~` for your home folder.

claudes.anonymiseAccounts.markdownDescription:
Hide who these accounts belong to, **in every window**. The eye at the top of the ClaudeS panel does the same for its own window only; while this setting is on, no window can show the names.

Accounts are listed as **Account 1**, **Account 2**, ... and signed-in addresses are masked as `o****@l****.com` — enough shape to recognise your own, not enough for anyone else. Folder paths are hidden too, since they carry the name.

For sharing a screen, presenting, or taking screenshots. Colours stay as they are: they identify a row to you and reveal nothing.

Terminals already open keep the name they were created with.

claudes.statusLine.markdownDescription:
Show the account and its plan usage at the bottom of each ClaudeS terminal: the 5-hour window, when it resets, the week, and how full the conversation's context is.

The figures come from Claude Code itself — ClaudeS reads no token and makes no network request for them. The status line is given to each session with `claude --settings`, so your Claude Code settings are not changed, and a status line you configured yourself is left in place. Needs `node` on your PATH.

Applies to terminals opened after the change.

claudes.usageOrangeFrom.markdownDescription: In the status line at the bottom of each terminal, the 5-hour and weekly usage turn **orange** from this percentage; below it they are green. Applies at once, also to terminals already open.

claudes.usageRedFrom.markdownDescription: In the status line at the bottom of each terminal, the 5-hour and weekly usage turn **red** from this percentage. Never below the orange one. Applies at once, also to terminals already open.

claudes.autoStartClaude.description: Run the 'claude' command automatically in the terminal opened when switching account. Turn off to get a ready terminal without starting Claude Code.

claudes.claudeCommand.description: Command used to start Claude Code in the terminal. Change it if the CLI is installed under a different name or path.

claudes.closeOtherProfileTerminals.markdownDescription:
Close terminals belonging to other accounts when opening a new one.

**Off** (default): accounts sit side by side. Some of a job on the client's account, some on your own, in the same project — each terminal keeps the account it was created with, named and coloured on its own tab.

**On**: only one account has a terminal open at a time.

enumDescriptions: Share automatically. A new account gets your permissions, MCP servers, skills and plugins.
Ask each time a new account is created.
Never share. Every account starts with a clean environment.
claudes.shareSetupWithNewAccounts.markdownDescription:
Permissions, MCP servers, skills and plugins live **inside each account folder**, so a brand new account starts without any of them — and every command asks for confirmation again.

This setting decides what happens when you create an account.

**Always** (default): the new account is linked to your main setup. Its login and its conversations stay its own. Anything you put in the shared settings, skills or plugins reaches every account that shares them.

**Ask**: choose per account. Useful when some clients have their own MCP servers and rules and others do not.

**Never**: every account is a clean, fully separate environment.

Credentials and chat history are *never* shared, whatever this is set to.

viewsWelcome.contents:
No accounts yet.

Each account is one Claude login with a folder of its own. Add one, sign in to it once, and from then on its + opens a terminal on it.

[Add an Account](command:claudes.newProfile)



Questions or problems? We recommend asking Claude first: the answer is usually in the documentation.

[Copy the Documentation for Claude](command:claudes.copyDocsForClaude)

Paste it into Claude and add your question. It is always in the … menu above, too.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: Accounts and credentials are read from your home folder, and the command that runs is an application-scoped setting a workspace cannot override.

virtualWorkspaces.description: ClaudeS runs the Claude Code CLI in a local terminal, so it needs a real filesystem.
